sections.text:
feat: lazy (non-blocking) managed-walletd — instant MCP handshake
In exfer-stack/exfer-mcp, his own repository.
https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-mcp/pull/4

Managed mode used to call `supervisor.start()` synchronously before serving, blocking the MCP handshake ~10-20s (Argon2 keystore unlock + walletd boot) while the agent host (codex) showed a frozen "starting" with no feedback.

## Lazy contract
- The MCP server answers the **handshake + list_tools INSTANTLY** (static tool defs; never awaits walletd). Bind port chosen synchronously; walletd spawned in a background asyncio task.
- `supervisor.ensure_ready()` resolves once walletd wrote its token + answered `get_block_height`. The tool-dispatch path awaits it before building the cached `AsyncClient` → the agent sees at most **one slow first call**, never a frozen handshake; a ready-timeout yields a clean error (not a hang).
- **Cleanup** on every exit path (atexit + SIGINT/SIGTERM + finally), incl. server-exits-before-ready → the spawning walletd is killed; the first-run `init-seeded` child is now tracked too so a stop mid-Argon2 leaves no lingering process.
- **External mode** (`WALLETD_URL` set) unchanged.

## Verified
- list_tools returns **22 tools in 0.1ms**, before the first walletd health check.
- Real run: handshake instant (walletd not ready) → first `exfer_get_block_height` boots walletd ~7s → **live height** → second call cached/fast.
- Cleanup: server exits before ready → spawning walletd terminated, **no orphan** (ps-confirmed).
- Gates: **pytest 56**, ruff, mypy green.

After this, managed mode is both self-starting AND non-blocking — codex connects instantly and walletd comes up under the first tool call.
